question: Under what concession is poison said not to enter the body?
premises: Poison is the subject of negation.
The negation is that it does not enter the body.
This holds even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body of the person in question.
uncertainties: The verse implies a prior condition on that person, but that condition is not stated here.
plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
